scope: the whole soldier: proportions, silhouette, placement, layering, the hold, and the first materials (values, colours, wear) against the reference; ignore fine surface detail

merged.text: The left hand does not hold the carbine: it lies flat on the handguard with straight fingers. Any shooter would see the support hand is not controlling the muzzle.
also: The left hand lies open over the handguard and does not hold the carbine; the reference grips from below with closed fingers.

The left hand rests open on top of the handguard with straight fingers pointing down the far side; it does not close on the carbine. The reference wraps the handguard from below with curled fingers and the thumb over.
Left hand lies palm-down on top of the handguard with straight, splayed fingers that never wrap it; no thumb opposes, so the hand is resting on the gun, not holding it.
fixes: Bring the palm under the handguard and curl all four fingers round it, thumb along the near side.
Cup the handguard from below as drawn: palm under the rail, fingers curled over the top, thumb along the near side, knuckles flexed about 60 to 90 degrees.

merged.text: The face is another man: broad, flat and square with a heavy brow bar, small eyes and orange skin, where the reference has a long lean face, high hairline, arched brows and hollow cheeks. Identity fails at a glance.
also: The face is not the reference man: wider and flatter, square forehead with a straight low hairline, heavy dark brow bar, small close-set eyes, short blunt nose, weak cheekbones and jaw definition, saturated orange skin.
fixes: The reference has a longer, narrower face, a higher M-shaped hairline, arched separate brows, deeper-set larger eyes, a longer straight nose, hollow cheeks and a tanned but neutral skin tone.

merged.text: The boots are low pale trainers with pointed toes; the reference has tall, dark, heavy laced combat boots with deep lugged soles.
also: The boots read as low, smooth trainers: short shaft, thin pointed toe, slim sole, pale grey panels. The reference has tall laced combat boots with a bulbous toe cap, deep lugged sole, heel block and dark scuffed leather.
The boots are low trainers with thin soles and pointed toes; a combat boot of this class has a mid shaft, chunky lugged sole and a rubber toe cap.

Boots read as low-cut trainers: shaft barely above the ankle, thin sole, long pointed toe with no bumper; the reference and a Zephyr-class mid boot have a shaft about 150 mm high, a chunky lugged sole and a rounded rubber toe cap.
The soldier's right boot reads as a low trainer with a swoosh upper and a thin sole; both boots lack the reference's chunky lugs and visible lacing.
The soldier's right boot reads as a low trainer: a smooth swoosh-panelled upper, low collar, few visible laces and a thin sole, unlike the reference's chunky lace-up boots with deep lugs.
fixes: Raise the shaft to mid-shin height under the trouser, deepen the toe box and the sole, darken the upper to near black.
Raise the shaft to mid-boot height, thicken the midsole and lugs, round and bulk the toe with a rubber rand.
Mid-height leather and textile upper with visible eyelets and laces to the collar, toe rand, and a thick lugged sole with a heel step.

merged.text: The carrier is a flat clean grey-olive; the reference is worn olive-khaki with dirt and edge abrasion. The kit reads unissued.
also: The carrier is too grey and too tidy: three identical pouches and a plain panel, against a warm worn olive carrier with unequal flapped pouches.

The carrier is a flat grey-olive with three identical smooth pouches and a plain chest panel; the reference carrier is a warmer coyote-olive, heavily worn, with a detailed chest panel and unequal flapped pouches.
Carrier and pouches are a flat, clean grey-olive; the reference carrier is olive-khaki Cordura with heavy edge wear, dirt and fading, and its colour shifts warmer than the render.
The carrier and pouches are clean blockout boxes in flat olive-grey; the reference's are worn tan-olive cordura with lumps, binding and dirt.

The carrier front and pouches read as clean blockout boxes: flat uniform olive-grey with no fabric weave, binding, wear or dirt, and pouch flaps as flat lids; the reference's carrier is worn tan-olive cordura.
fixes: Shift the carrier hue toward yellow-olive, raise saturation, and vary the pouch row as drawn.
Warm the base toward olive-khaki, add abrasion on edges and pouch lids, dust in recesses and fading on the top surfaces.
Cordura weave at real scale, bound edges, the reference's tan-olive hue, scuffs and dirt on edges, pouch flaps with thickness and sag.

merged.text: The hair is a tall spiked crest that runs out of the frame; the reference is a short textured crop with faded sides.
also: The hair stands in a tall spiked crest that leaves the top of the frame, like a mohawk, with dense dark sides; the reference is a short textured crop about 30 mm high with a faded side.
The hair is a mohawk-like crest of cones that breaks the top of the silhouette.
Hair is a crest of spiky cones on a shaved scalp, a mohawk tuft that breaks the head silhouette; the reference has short textured hair with front volume and short but covered sides.
fixes: Shorten the crown strands to a few centimetres, lay them forward and sideways in clumps, and fade the sides to stubble length.
Clumped short strands swept up and to one side at the front, tapering to short coverage over the sides and back.

merged.text: [D2] The hold is not a hold: the right hand is a loose fist beside the pistol grip and the left hand drapes stiff fingers over the rail. Real hands wrap, with the palm pressed to the gun.
also: Right hand does not close on the pistol grip: middle, ring and little fingers curl into a loose fist beside the grip with air inside, the index finger lies straight along the receiver; the hand hovers rather than grips.
fixes: Wrap the three lower fingers fully round the grip with the web of the hand high in the grip's tang, palm in contact; index along the lower receiver above the trigger guard.

merged.text: Skin is orange and waxy, which reads as CG before anything else in the frame; the reference skin is a desaturated, weathered tan.
also: Skin is a saturated orange, uniform and waxy, with no redness variation at nose, cheeks and ears and no paler stubble zone; the reference skin is a desaturated, weathered tan.
fixes: Lower saturation, add regional colour zones (redder nose and ears, bluish beard shadow) and specular breakup.

merged.text: The shirt is a neoprene skin: smooth, seamless, slightly shiny sleeves and torso. Real combat shirts gather at the elbows and under straps and show seams and weave.
also: The combat shirt reads as a neoprene wetsuit: seamless smooth sleeves and torso with a slight sheen, no folds, seams, cuffs or cloth weave anywhere on the arms or chest.
fixes: Matte woven cloth with seams down the sleeve, gathering at the elbow crook and under straps, fabric texture at native scale.

merged.text: Pauldrons and forearm guards are pale clean grey plastic; the reference armour is dark and worn, so the arms jump out of the value structure.
also: Pauldrons and forearm guards are pale, clean grey reading as plastic; the reference armour is dark grey-olive, scuffed to bright metal-like edges.
fixes: Darken the base value markedly, keep wear to edges and raised areas.

merged.text: The armour plates are light grey plastic with painted edge streaks; the reference's are dark gunmetal with chipped, dirty wear. The value jump makes the kit read toy-like.
also: Armour plates (pauldrons, upper-arm and forearm guards) are light grey plastic, far lighter than the reference's dark gunmetal; wear is only painted streaks along the edges.
fixes: Darker painted-metal or polymer value near the reference's, wear as chips and scuffs on high points and edges with dirt in recesses.

merged.text: [D6] Hard armour behaves like cloth: the pauldron is dented and wobbly with rolled rims, and the forearm guards are inflated stacked cylinders instead of thin shells following the forearm.
also: The right pauldron is a flat bent sheet with wobbly, dented surfaces and soft rolled rims, like crumpled cloth rather than a rigid moulded shell; its outer edge stands well off the arm.
fixes: A rigid moulded shell: smooth continuous curvature, crisp chamfered edges, consistent thickness, seated on the shoulder with its strap pulling it in.

merged.text: The trousers below the knee are narrow smooth tubes with a straight hem and a thin ankle showing; the reference is baggy, panelled and bloused over the boots.
also: The lower trousers are smooth narrow tubes ending in a straight hem above the boot; the reference trousers are baggy, with reinforced shin panels, stacked folds and the cuffs bloused over the boot tops.
fixes: Add cloth volume below the knee, the lighter shin reinforcement panels, and gather the hem onto the boot collar.

merged.text: The right pauldron is a flat board standing off the shoulder and rising above it, breaking the shoulder silhouette; real plates are domed and seated on the deltoid.
also: Right pauldron is a flat board hanging from the shoulder strap, standing off the deltoid and rising above the shoulder line; real shoulder armour is domed to follow the deltoid and sits on it.
fixes: Curve the plate around the deltoid cap, seat it on the sleeve, and hang it from the carrier shoulder strap so its top sits at the acromion, not above it.

merged.text: The face is orange and waxy with a uniform sheen and painted-on brows; it reads as a game asset next to the reference's weathered skin.
also: Skin is saturated orange and waxy with flat shading and a broad uniform sheen; eyebrows are dark painted bars with hard lower edges; the temple silhouette on the viewer's right is a straight vertical cut.
fixes: Less saturated, varied skin tone (redder cheeks and nose, cooler jaw under stubble), breakup in the specular, hair-strand brows, a rounded temple.

merged.text: The arm armour is light clean grey; the reference plates are dark gunmetal with tan worn edges, near the shirt in value. The diff map is white across every plate.
also: The arm armour is a clean light grey, far lighter than the reference (white in the diff): the drawn plates are dark gunmetal with tan worn edges and olive-brown grime, close in value to the shirt.
fixes: Drop the plates' base value by about half and warm it; keep bright values only on worn edges.

merged.text: A dark sock gap shows between trouser hem and boot collar; trousers break over the boot or blouse into it, never stop short.
also: Trouser hem ends above the boot collar, leaving a dark band of sock or ankle; real trousers either break over the boot top or are bloused into it.
fixes: Lengthen the hem so it rests on the boot upper with a break and stacked folds, as the reference shows.

merged.text: The face scowls under low brows on a flat forehead with a very wide square jaw; the head reads boxy and heavier than the reference man.
also: Brows sit low on the upper lids in a scowl over a flat, slab forehead with no frontal eminences or temple hollows; the jaw reads very wide and square, making the head boxy.
fixes: Raise the brows to sit on the orbital rim, model the frontal bossing and temporal fossa, narrow the gonial angles.

merged.text: The gloves are smooth rubber mitts with sausage fingers, no knuckle pads or seams.
also: Gloves read as smooth rubber mitts: equal sausage fingers, no knuckle pads, panel seams, palm wrinkles or fabric texture; the reference shows padded M-Pact type gloves.
fixes: Model the knuckle and finger armour pads, panel seams, fourchettes and bunching at the knuckles; give the backhand a synthetic textile and the palm a suede-like value.

merged.text: The right hand does not read as closed on a pistol grip, and both gloves are bare-hand shapes without padding or cuffs.
also: The right hand is a thin bare-hand shape in a glove colour, lying against the receiver with no visible wrap of a pistol grip; the reference glove is bulky, with knuckle padding and a broad cuff under the forearm guard.
fixes: Close the lower three fingers round the grip with the web high on the backstrap, and give the glove its padded thickness.

merged.text: The hair is a spiky crest over shaved sides, a mohawk, rather than the reference's short textured crop with haired sides.
also: Hair is a spiky upright crest over clean shaved sides, reading as a mohawk; the reference has a short textured crop, top swept up and back, sides short but haired.
fixes: Keep a few millimetres of hair on the sides tapering to the ears and lay the top longer and swept back.

merged.text: The shirt is skin-tight over the back, shoulders and arms; the reference shirt has ease, seams and folds.
also: The shirt follows every muscle of the back and upper arms like paint; the reference shirt is a loose combat shirt with seams, sleeve folds and its own thickness.
fixes: Give the shirt ease over the shoulders and arms so it bridges the muscle forms and folds at the elbow and armpit.

merged.text: The lower trousers are straight pipes with no stacking over the boots, and the camo is blurred blotch noise rather than a printed pattern with dirt.
also: Lower trouser legs are straight smooth pipes with no stacking or blousing over the boot, and the camo is large blurred low-frequency blotches that read as a smudged noise texture, not a printed pattern with dirt.
fixes: Cloth stacking and bunching above the boot collar, sharper printed pattern at real scale over a near-black base, dirt concentrated at the hems and knees.

merged.text: The left upper-arm plates stop short and leave a long bare sleeve above the elbow; the drawn plates and olive band nearly reach the elbow.
also: The left upper-arm armour ends about a third of the way up from the elbow, leaving a long bare sleeve; the reference stacks a pauldron and a long second plate with an olive band that reach nearly to the elbow.
fixes: Lengthen the lower plate and add the olive wrap so the armour covers the upper arm as drawn.

merged.text: The left sleeve balloons at the elbow point instead of stretching over it and gathering in the crook.
also: Left sleeve balloons into a large rounded bulge at the elbow point; a bent sleeve stretches over the olecranon and gathers in the crook, it does not inflate outward.
fixes: Pull the sleeve taut over the elbow point and bunch the slack into the inner crook.

merged.text: Seen from behind, the trousers cling to the seat like leggings, at odds with the baggy legs below.
also: The trousers cling to the buttocks and hamstrings like leggings, showing glute anatomy, inconsistent with the baggy legs below.
fixes: Stiff trouser cloth hanging from the seat with ease, folds radiating from the crotch and under the belt.

merged.text: The knee pads are plain boxes with a hexagon, proud of the leg; the drawn caps are faceted shields in a tan frame with side wings.
also: The knee pads are plain rounded boxes with a raised hexagon, standing proud of the leg; the reference pads have a faceted shield-shaped cap in a tan frame with side wings, seated on a dark padded backing.
fixes: Shape the cap as a tapering faceted shield, add the frame and wings, and seat it into the backing.

merged.text: Knee pads are flat boxes sitting proud of the leg with one strap; real pads curve around the knee.
also: Knee pads are flat-faced boxes standing proud of the trouser, with only one visible strap; AirFlex-class pads are curved shells that wrap the patella and sit in a knee pocket or under two straps.
fixes: Curve the cap around the knee, seat it into the trouser knee, and show the upper and lower straps.

merged.text: A skin-coloured patch shows at the left shoulder beside the strap, under the antenna.
also: A skin-coloured orange-brown patch shows at the left shoulder beside the carrier strap, below the antenna, where there should be only shirt and strap.
fixes: Find what is showing through (the body through the shirt, or an unassigned material) and cover or correct it.

merged.text: Left hand's fingers lie stiff and evenly spaced over the top of the handguard like a claw, no thumb visible under or beside it, fingertips appear to sit into the rail teeth.
fixes: Close the hand round the handguard: thumb along the side or over the top, fingers wrapped under, palm pressing the side, fingertips resting on the surface, not in it.

merged.text: Forearm guards (both arms, right shown) are fat stacked cylinders like rolled cuffs, wider than the forearm and not tapering to the wrist; the reference's guards are contoured plates following the forearm.
fixes: Shells that follow the forearm's taper and flattened cross-section, thin-walled, strapped close, segmented where the reference shows segments.

merged.text: A hard ring above the left elbow where the simulated upper sleeve stops over the lower sleeve gives away two separate meshes.
also: Hard stepped ring above the left elbow where the simulated upper sleeve ends over the lower sleeve: a clean lip with a dark gap, like two separate tubes.
fixes: One continuous sleeve, folds gathering into the elbow crook rather than a seam-like step.

merged.text: The front mag pouches are wide pudgy blocks rather than narrow, taller flapped M4 pouches.
also: Mag pouches are wide, pudgy blocks butted together; real triple M4 pouches are narrow (about 75 mm each) and taller, with flaps or bungee retention and visible spacing on the PALS.
fixes: Narrow each pouch to one STANAG width plus wall, raise its height, add the flap or bungee.

merged.text: Knee pads are soft pillows with clean surfaces instead of rigid faceted caps, and the strap behind the right knee stands off the leg.
also: Knee pads are soft pillow shells with a uniform clean surface; the strap and buckle behind the soldier's right knee stand off the leg.
fixes: Rigid faceted caps with crisp edges and scuffs, straps pulled tight into the trouser cloth.

merged.text: The right thigh cases have bright tan faces; the drawn ones are dark throughout.
also: The right thigh rig's two cases have bright tan faces on black bodies; in the reference the cases are dark grey-black with only faint tan wear, and read as one dark mass.
fixes: Darken the case faces to near the body colour and keep tan for worn edges only.

merged.text: Two stray wire hooks hang under the right drop-leg panel.
also: Two thin wire-like hooks dangle under the drop-leg panel with nothing to attach to.
fixes: Remove them or make them the panel's lower leg-strap buckle ends.

merged.text: Two wire hooks dangle under the soldier's right drop-leg pouch, and the thigh straps are perfect flat bands round a cylinder.
also: Thigh straps wrap the leg as perfect flat bands with no compression or wrinkling of the trouser cloth beneath; two wire hooks dangle under the drop-leg pouch.
fixes: Straps cinch into the cloth with gathers either side; hooks either tucked or removed.

merged.text: The whole figure reads as an athlete in a tight suit with plates attached, not the reference's bulky layered soldier. The mass of cloth and kit is well under the drawing on the arms, hips and legs.
Sleeves are smooth inflated tubes: the arms read bodybuilder-thick while the reference is lean with armour giving the bulk.
Straps sit on every surface without biting into it: no compression, gathers or contact shadow under the arm, thigh and knee straps, so each item looks pasted on rather than worn.
In the side views the carbine is carried at arm's length well in front of the carrier; the reference low ready keeps it closer to the body.
The right pauldron sits higher and further outboard than drawn and is a single smooth plate; the reference has a smaller cap with a second plate under it running down the arm.
Gloves read as smooth rubber with no knuckle protection or seams; Mechanix M-Pact class gloves have moulded knuckle guards visible at this size.
Mass reads wrong: inflated arms and cuffs but a thin, flat-faced carrier with empty-looking pouches, where the reference is lean in the body and heavy in the kit.
The gaiter is a tall smooth cowl of one value; the reference is a thinner scarf with deep irregular folds that sits lower on the neck and tucks inside the carrier straps.
The legs are straight locked columns with no calf or knee shape showing through the cloth, which stiffens the stance next to the reference's.
The trouser cloth is a uniform brown-grey with soft blotches; the reference is darker, nearly black in the folds, with strong lighter wear on the thighs and shins.
Trouser upper legs read close to tights around the crotch while the lower legs are wide straight tubes; Crye G3 class cut is roomier above and tapers below.
The stock hangs in front of the right chest without clear contact with the arm or the carrier; in a real low ready it rests against the chest or under the arm.
The emblem is a bright white star on mid blue; the reference is a duller pale crossed mark on a dark slate shield, less contrast and a different figure.
The carbine is uniformly clean matte black with no edge wear, next to a heavily worn reference gun, so it reads as a fresh model rather than a used rifle.

The carbine, though declared real, reads slim and toy-clean against the hands: a matte black with no wear and tan flecks only, where the drawn gun is worn grey metal with tan parts. Its value is too uniform.
